newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KNPC plans new oil port at al-Ahmadi - report.
newsitem.headline: KNPC plans new oil port at al-Ahmadi - report.

text.p: State oil refiner Kuwait National Petroleum Co (KNPC) plans to build a new oil loading port at the al-Ahmadi refinery, a newspaper reported on Monday.
"There are intentions to build a new large port at Ahmadi that applies modern technology," Abdul-Rahman al-Taweel, KNPC's deputy managing director, told al-Anba in an interview.
"It has been decided that consultants will be appointed...to start studies for establishing a port that follows the enormous development in the tankers industry," he said.
Taweel did not give details about the planned project.
KNPC also plans to build an oil products loading pier to replace the Gulf War-damaged south pier at Ahmadi, he said. The planned pier would be operational in September 2002, he said.
"The cost for repairing the south pier would be very high therefore a project to establish a new pier has been approved."
Many of Kuwait's oil industry facilities were damaged during the 1990-91 seven-month Iraqi occupation.
KNPC is the refining arm of state-owned oil conglomerate Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) which supervises the Gulf Arab state's oil industry.
